answer: Latency-delta admission gating. Each agent's routing peer set must show a copper-bottomed consistency: round-trip times to its declared neighbors stay within a measured delta of historical medians over sliding windows. Clones spun up in one datacenter produce near-identical latency vectors, a crystal-clear signature, so admission requires each identity's neighbor-latency profile to deviate independently. An attacker must rent genuinely dispersed network positions per clone, paying real hosting and route-diversity costs that scale linearly with each added identity.
